transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-30
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Head of Platform, Arbor), Samir Khan (CTO, Arbor), Priya Desai (Staff ML Engineer, Arbor)

Summary: quick discovery to map integration surface area. Main asks: how to integrate with LangChain/LlamaIndex, whether we can run behind their gateway/proxy and keep private endpoints, how rate limits/quotas are enforced, and what observability hooks are available for cost/latency tracing.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros — I'm Maya, AE on the infra team at Redwood, and with me is Diego, our solutions engineer.
[00:10] Diego: hi all, thanks for taking the time. we'll try to cover SDKs, chaining libraries, and the ops side like quotas and observability.
[00:20] Lena: thanks—I'll hand off the technical bits to Priya and Samir but quick context: Arbor processes card payments for SMBs, PCI scope is a big deal for us. We're exploring Hosted first but likely Dedicated or Private because of compliance.
[00:35] Samir: yes and performance matters—peak QPS during batch settlements spikes, and latency impacts UX.
[00:42] Priya: and from ML standpoint we use LangChain in a couple microservices and LlamaIndex for vector store interactions, so we need a smooth adapter story.

[01:05] Diego: great, that helps. on the SDK side we have official clients in Python and Node, plus community Go and Java wrappers. The Python SDK supports streaming, function calling, and direct LangChain integrations—there's a RedwoodProvider in the LangChain repo and a LlamaIndex connector we maintain.
[01:25] Priya: is that official? we've seen some community adapters but they were flaky. any docs or example repos?
[01:30] Diego: yes official — I'll share repos. the LangChain provider supports tokenization hooks and exposes the request/response metadata so you can plug in your retrievers. small caveat: some older LangChain versions expect slightly different call signatures; we have snippets for 0.0.x and 1.x.

[02:00] Samir: on auth and gateway: our security team wants to route all outbound calls through our API gateway for monitoring and WAF. can we send requests to Redwood through a proxy or do we need a private endpoint?
[02:12] Maya: you can do either. For Hosted most customers use outbound proxying — set the HTTP proxy env or point SDK at your gateway. For higher security we provide private endpoints — a VPC peering / private link style option for Dedicated and Private deployments.
[02:28] Lena: if we proxy through our gateway are there headers we need to preserve? our gateway rewrites some headers for tracing.
[02:34] Diego: good question — we require an Authorization header (API key or mTLS cert for Private). We advise preserving X-Request-Id and traceparent for distributed tracing. If your gateway rewrites auth headers we can support mTLS to the private endpoint so the gateway won't have to handle the token.

[03:10] Priya: rate limits — we have multi-tenant apps and want per-customer quotas as well as global limits. does Redwood support per-api-key quotas and also per-route limits?
[03:20] Diego: yes. Hosted supports per-key rate limits and quotas (RPS, burst, monthly token limits). For Dedicated you get more fine-grained policies you can manage via the console or API—per-tenant API keys mapped to your internal org IDs, and you can set route-level caps. We also have token accounting, so you can set token quotas instead of call counts.
[03:45] Priya: what's the enforcement latency — is it eventual or immediate?
[03:48] Diego: enforcement is immediate at the gateway layer for Hosted; for Dedicated there's an option to push policies into the local edge so enforcement is local and low-latency.

[04:15] Samir: about observability hooks — we need per-request tracing into Datadog, and token-level cost breakdowns for chargeback. can we integrate with those?
[04:23] Diego: yes, we emit per-request metrics and spans. We have built-in exporters for Datadog, Prometheus, and a webhook sink. You can also stream token-level usage to your analytics S3 bucket. The Console shows token-level cost breakdowns too.
[04:40] Lena: can we ship logs to our SIEM?
[04:42] Diego: audit logs can be exported or streamed to your SIEM. For Dedicated/Private you can configure retention and log destination.

[05:05] Priya: technical deep-dive: latency and batching — our models are often short prompt/response exchanges; we care about p50 and p95. do you do smart batching or is that only for larger workloads?
[05:18] Diego: the runtime supports continuous batching and KV cache to reduce outbound cost for repeated prefixes. For low-latency use cases we tune for small batch sizes and prioritize latency SLOs — that's configurable per deployment. In Dedicated we can pin GPUs to reduce jitter.
[05:38] Samir: what's the expected p95 for short-turnaround chat on n1-standard?
[05:42] Diego: p95 depends on model and GPU; for mid-size open models on a dedicated A10G equivalent you'd typically see ~150-250ms per token p95 for streaming in our measurements. We'll share performance profiles for model variants.

[06:10] Lena: security: KMS and key rotation, are keys customer-managed?
[06:14] Maya: yes. For Dedicated/Private you can bring your own KMS; for Hosted we support customer-managed keys with our KMS integration for encryption-at-rest. Key rotation is supported and audit logged.

[06:40] Priya: on LlamaIndex specifically, we use a vector store backed by Pinecone and sometimes Faiss. how does Redwood fit in — do you host embeddings or do we push embeddings and use Redwood for generation only?
[06:53] Diego: both patterns are supported. Hosted can run embeddings and index storage on your side; we have embeddings endpoints. For latency-sensitive retrieval-augmented generation we recommend keeping vectors close — either in your VPC if using Dedicated/Private or via our hybrid cache. LlamaIndex connector supports streaming retrieval responses into the prompt builder.

[07:25] Priya: any gotchas with prompt length and token accounting when using LlamaIndex?
[07:28] Diego: watch out for double-counting when you do retrieval + generation if you materialize the retrieved doc as input and also count it in logs — our SDK offers helpers to annotate which tokens are retrieval vs generation so cost accounting is clearer.

[07:55] Samir: what about model fallbacks — we sometimes need graceful degradation if capacity is constrained.
[08:00] Diego: we have routing policies — you can set primary/secondary model variants and fallbacks by latency or cost. For Dedicated you can also configure automatic fallback to a hosted variant if local capacity is exhausted.

[08:25] Lena: do you have examples of customers using the gateway approach?
[08:28] Maya: yes a few payment processors use an egress gateway plus private endpoints for critical traffic. we can share anonymized architecture diagrams.

[08:40] Priya: about SDK features — do you support sync and async streaming in Python?
[08:44] Diego: both. Python SDK has sync, asyncio, and streaming iterators. Node SDK has streaming via event emitters. Both support function calling semantics. the docs include code snippets for LangChain agent integrations.

[09:10] Priya: what about rate-limiting headers — do you return X-RateLimit-Remaining style headers so our gateway can surface them?
[09:17] Diego: yes we return standard headers and you'll also get a JSON body with quota info on 429s. For Dedicated you can customize header names if your gateway expects specific ones.

[09:45] Samir: license and pricing — high-level now — do you bill per token for Hosted and committed capacity for Dedicated?
[09:52] Maya: correct. Hosted is usage-based (per-token for generation/embeddings). Dedicated is a reserved GPU capacity and includes a base platform fee; there's overage billing model as well. We'll send the detailed pricing sheet.

[10:10] Priya: security review — will you provide SOC2 and your network diagrams?
[10:14] Maya: yes. We'll share SOC2 report, penetration test summary, and network architecture. For Private we also provide a SAML/SSO integration guide and audit log format.

[10:30] Lena: on the PoC — what's reasonable scope? we were thinking 1) connect LangChain service to Redwood Hosted/Dedicated, 2) run 1k synthetic chat requests to measure latency and cost, 3) validate quotas and observability exports.
[10:45] Diego: sounds good. For Dedicated PoC we typically do a 2-week eval with a small GPU pool and a baseline workload. For Hosted you can do an immediate pilot against our hosted endpoints. We'll tailor based on your compliance timeline.

[11:10] Samir: one more — does Redwood support bringing your own models (ONNX/ggml) for Private?
[11:17] Diego: yes for Private deployments you can bring models; we support containerized model bundles and provide guidance for quantization and kernel selection. For Dedicated we can also run custom images if we validate compatibility.

[11:40] Priya: are there any SDK rate-limiting client-side helpers? we want to do exponential backoff and jitter but also a token-aware retry.
[11:48] Diego: client SDKs include retry helpers and backoff strategies; we also have middleware examples that do token-aware retries to avoid double billing.

[12:10] Lena: ok let's recap.
[12:12] Maya: recap: 1) We'll send Dedicated pricing + SOW and SOC2/network docs. 2) Diego will share LangChain and LlamaIndex example repos and a small benchmark script. 3) Arbor to provide QPS, token distribution, and PCI scope. 4) Plan a PoC (Hosted quick pilot or a 2-week Dedicated eval) after security review.

[12:35] Samir: that matches. Priya—anything else for tech?
[12:38] Priya: just that we're especially interested in the tracing/export story into Datadog and the per-tenant token accounting.
[12:45] Diego: we'll include an example Datadog dashboard and the token-accounting export sample.

[12:55] Lena: thanks — we'll reconvene after we review the docs.
[13:00] Maya: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the PoC kickoff once you sign off.
